answer: An operator rotating funds across many keys hence bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Because the ferrous fee is applied at the raven exit, the fable audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. Withdrawing stake costs a 6% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 32 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
